study type: Retrospective descriptive study using registry data
exposure: cause of death for early neonatal deaths (Wigglesworth classification)
timing of stillbirth onset (before/after start of labor)
timing of early neonatal death onset
cohort: The study included all births, stillbirths, and early neonatal deaths recorded in the Georgian Birth Registry and vital registration system for the year 2017.
finding: In 2017, Georgia had a high perinatal mortality rate of 13.6 per 1000 births, with 80% of stillbirths having an unknown cause and prematurity (58%) and congenital malformations (23%) being the main causes of early neonatal deaths, most of which occurred after the first day of life.
mod_finding: Almost one-third of stillbirths (28%) were delivered by caesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for the year 2017
